answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity bond paid before an address can claim work. Each new agent escrows stake slashed if ejected for duplicate or low-quality output, so farming identities means locking real capital per key. Payout is capped per address while bond cost is not shared: a thousand keys cost a thousand bonds yet earn only a handful of marginal rewards, cost rising like an ocean swell while each fake key sinks like a marble. A whisper of collusion does not lower locked stake, and the emission ceiling makes extra identities dilute the pool.
